clue.text: Highest money for those in authority

parts.note: the highest point is the top
brass is northern British slang for cash

explanation.surface: A complaint that the biggest salaries go to the people in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass meaning money is everyday British slang, as in 'where there's muck there's brass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Top brass is an idiom for the senior officers or executives of an organisation.

clue.text: Attempt to secure one pound for a du Maurier novel

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so one piece encloses others

parts.note: an attempt is a try
the Roman numeral for one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Trying to buy a du Maurier novel for a single pound.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel is by George du Maurier (1894), whose heroine gave her name to the hat, not by his granddaughter Daphne.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilby is the title of George du Maurier's novel about an artist's model and Svengali.

clue.text: Mischief-maker, almost drunk

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: pickled is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A troublemaker who is nearly intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickle is a playful word for a naughty child, a little rascal.

clue.text: Skate in narrow beam of light

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flat fish of the same family as the skate
second meaning: a thin shaft of light

explanation.surface: Someone skating along through a thin shaft of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray is both a flat cartilaginous fish, of which the skate is one, and a line of light.

clue.text: Held a demonstration with foreign despot as target

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so these letters appear in an altered form

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Marchers rallied against a tyrant from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage a protest is to organise a public demonstration against something.

clue.text: Ancient city member in South America

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other, so the member sits inside

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for South America
a member is a part of a body or whole

explanation.surface: A tourist note about an old city found on another continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was the militaristic city-state of ancient Greece, rival to Athens.

clue.text: Certain costermongers in shocking pink argyles

indicators.note: a shock jolts things out of place, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Street traders dressed in garish pink diamond-patterned socks.
explanation.walkthrough: Costermongers are London street sellers of fruit and veg; argyles are diamond-patterned socks or jumpers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearly kings are London costermongers' leaders who wear suits covered in pearl buttons for charity events.

clue.text: Quick and energetic, and extraordinarily good

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a dated British intensifier

explanation.walkthrough: The first 'and' belongs to the first meaning; the second joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a brisk pace and, in old-fashioned British usage, something very fine indeed.

clue.text: Heinous act at Petrograd, say, involving soldiers after revolution

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the others

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
Petrograd, the old name of St Petersburg, is an example of a city

explanation.surface: An outrage in revolutionary Russia with troops involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The Russian setting makes 'revolution' look historical; it signals a turnaround of the soldiers, who then sit between the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is an extremely wicked or cruel deed, especially one involving violence.

clue.text: Complaint got by one failing to keep joint dry?

definitions.text: Complaint got by one failing to keep joint dry?

parts.words: Complaint got by one failing to keep joint dry?
parts.note: surface reading: someone who cannot keep a place dry, perhaps a spilled-drink pub or a leaky building
setter's reading: the joint is a body joint in the leg, and the complaint is fluid collecting there

explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a pub or a cut of meat; here it is the body part that bends the leg, and 'complaint' is a medical one.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the everyday name for swelling caused by fluid build-up around the kneecap, an ailment.

clue.text: Unable to relax in it, church close to Ely

parts.note: taken as written
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

indicators.note: what lies close to the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of the cathedral city's name

explanation.surface: Someone restless inside a church near the English cathedral city of Ely.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire; only its final letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being itchy, in its figurative sense, means restless and impatient, unable to settle.

clue.text: White stone in altar base, cracked

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A church inspection finds pale stone in a damaged altar foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a soft, fine-grained translucent mineral, typically white, used for carving.

clue.text: What can make you be so long adding drop of espagnole sauce?

indicators.note: the question asks what these letters can be made into, inviting a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a drop is the smallest amount, so just the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the French sauce's name

explanation.surface: A cook wondering which sauce takes so long once a little espagnole is stirred in.
explanation.walkthrough: Espagnole is a classic brown French sauce, so the surface stays in the kitchen while only one letter of it is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolognese is the meat-and-tomato pasta sauce named after Bologna.

clue.text: Ascend during fog and vanish

parts.note: to ascend is to go up
in means during, as in 'in the night'
smoke is a thick fog of fumes

explanation.surface: A climber rises through the mist and disappears from view.
explanation.definitionFit: To go up in smoke is an idiom for disappearing completely or coming to nothing.

clue.text: Ring back about one supplying tree

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read from right to left
about means going around, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Phoning someone back about a single tree being delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: CALL goes around I between its two Ls, and the whole is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a small flowering tree or shrub with fragrant purple or white blossoms.

clue.text: Quiten down tailored suit with pink coat?

indicators.note: tailored clothing is cut and reshaped, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tailor's instructions for a made-to-measure suit and a pink coat.
explanation.walkthrough: A pink coat is the scarlet coat worn in fox hunting, which keeps the surface in the world of clothes. 'Quiten' is the clue's spelling of quieten.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Put a sock in it' is a British slang imperative telling someone to be quiet.

clue.text: Chapter on mob after second game

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
c is short for chapter
a rabble is a disorderly mob

explanation.surface: A book chapter about a crowd, coming after a second instalment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts chapter in front of mob, and 'after second' puts the whole after the abbreviation for second.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is the board game of making words from lettered tiles.

clue.text: Opposition of French intended

parts.note: de is French for of
one's intended is the person one is engaged to

explanation.surface: Resistance from a French person's betrothed.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance or bold disobedience, a form of opposing someone.

clue.text: Trust able seaman? A loan may depend on it

definitions.text: A loan may depend on it

parts.note: to credit someone is to trust or believe them
an able seaman is an example of a rating, a sailor below officer rank

explanation.surface: Can you trust a sailor? A bank deciding on a loan might ask.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Royal Navy a rating is any enlisted sailor, and the question mark flags that an able seaman is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender checks a borrower's creditworthiness score before approving a loan, so the definition is descriptive.

clue.text: Lapses surrounding old university exam

indicators.note: surrounding means placed all round, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: lapses or slips are trips
o is short for old

explanation.surface: Slip-ups during an old-fashioned university examination.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tripos is the honours degree examination at Cambridge University.

clue.text: Fleet branch supported by a US lawyer

parts.note: an arm is a branch of an organisation or tree
taken as written
a District Attorney is a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: A naval branch backed by an American attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supported by' puts the first piece on top of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Novelist's wrong

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, British novelists
the possessive ending, taken as written

explanation.surface: A judgement that some writer has made a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive on 'Novelist's' supplies its own letter after the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss is an adjective meaning not right or faulty, as in 'something is amiss'.

clue.text: Club official, person much valued at end of year

parts.note: a highly valued person is called a treasure

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A club honours a much-loved official at its year-end gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is the officer of a club or society who manages its funds.

clue.text: Dramatist in Bonn working with Jones

indicators.note: something working is in motion and being processed, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A playwright collaborating with someone called Jones in the German city of Bonn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is part of the wordplay here, joining the two pieces of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Jonson was an English Jacobean playwright, author of Volpone and The Alchemist.

clue.text: Greek character, the brightest star

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the first letter of the Greek alphabet
second meaning: astronomers label a constellation's brightest star with this letter

explanation.surface: A Greek person described as the most brilliant celebrity around.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is both a Greek letter and the designation for the principal star in a constellation, as in Alpha Centauri.

clue.text: A quiet wood

parts.note: taken as written
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A peaceful woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a hardwood timber from the ash tree, used for tool handles.

clue.text: Level, holding the Parisian football team

indicators.note: holding means gripping something inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: level and even both mean flat or equal
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Scores level, with a Paris team involved.
explanation.definitionFit: A football side fields eleven players, so a team is commonly called an eleven.

clue.text: Chapel H.E. Bates unfortunately died inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other
an unfortunate outcome is things going awry, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the author's name taken letter by letter
d is the standard abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: The novelist H.E. Bates sadly passed away inside a chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: H.E. Bates wrote The Darling Buds of May; his name is fodder, and D goes inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethesda is a common name for a Nonconformist chapel, especially in Wales, after the biblical pool.
